11.title: Trading Activity and Price Movement by Market Cluster
11.alt: Market-level recorded trading activity per day versus price movement per hour, both log-transformed and standardized. Colors show the k = 3 assignments fitted using six features. Black X markers show those fitted cluster centroids projected onto the two displayed axes.

12.title: Hierarchical: Clusters = 3
12.alt: Average-linkage hierarchical clustering with cosine distance on six standardized features. A horizontal cut marks the three-group comparison.

13.title: Feature Distributions Before and After Preparation
13.alt: Seven rows compare original candidate feature distributions with values after selected log transformations and standardization.

14.title: Correlations Between Prepared Candidate Features
14.alt: Pearson correlations among seven prepared candidate features, including the strong positive correlation between distinct wallets and wallet trade count.

15.title: Silhouette Comparison
15.alt: Mean Euclidean silhouette scores for k-means with k from 2 to 8 on six standardized market features; k=1 has no defined silhouette score.

16.title: Elbow Method for k
16.alt: Within-cluster sum of squared distances for k-means with k from 1 to 8.

17.title: K-means Cluster Profiles
17.alt: Mean standardized feature values for the k=2 and k=3 market clusters, with cluster sizes shown beside each row.

18.title: Hierarchical: Clusters = 3
18.alt: Average-linkage hierarchical clustering with cosine distance on six standardized features. A horizontal cut marks the three-group comparison.

19.title: Agreement Between Clustering Methods
19.alt: Counts of markets grouped by k-means and hierarchical cluster. Hierarchical columns are ordered 2, 1, 3 to align the strongest overlaps on the diagonal; adjusted Rand index is 0.487.
19.subtitle: Adjusted Rand Index = 0.487

20.title: Cluster-Topic Correspondence
20.alt: Within-topic percentages and counts for the retained three k-means clusters. Sports: 7.6, 30.5, and 61.8 percent; Politics: 53.8, 39.6, and 6.6 percent; Economics: 39.6, 43.3, and 17.1 percent. Cluster descriptions summarize relative activity, certainty, and price movement.

21.title: Viewing Markets in Principal Component Space
21.alt: PC1-PC2 scatterplot of 492 markets, colored by Sports, Politics and Economics. The axes explain 53.6 and 21.4 percent of total variance, respectively.

22.title: Principal Component Directions
22.alt: Diagram of observations in two original feature dimensions, with PC1 along the greatest variation and PC2 perpendicular to PC1, intersecting at the data mean. Source: Dr. Osita Onyejekwe, course materials.

23.title: Cumulative Variance Explained by PCA
23.alt: Cumulative explained variance for one through seven principal components. Four components retain 95.3 percent, exceeding the dashed 90 percent threshold.

24.title: PCA Component Loadings
24.alt: Loadings of seven market features on PC1 through PC4, computed as component weights multiplied by square roots of eigenvalues. Red denotes positive relationships and blue denotes negative relationships.

25.title: PCA Biplot: PC1 and PC2
25.alt: Markets projected onto PC1 and PC2, colored by topic, with seven numbered component-weight arrows enlarged for visibility. PC1 and PC2 explain 53.6 and 21.4 percent of variance.
